newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Senate panel approves Tenet as CIA chief.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Senate panel approves Tenet as CIA chief.

text.p: The Senate Select Committee on Intelligence on Thursday unanimously approved the nomination of George Tenet to head the CIA, clearing the way for a confirmation vote by the full Senate.

The panel voted 19-0 in a closed meeting to approve President Bill Clinton's nominee after the Justice Department concluded a preliminary investigation of Tenet and saw no need to appoint an independent counsel.
The investigation covered Tenet's failure to disclose certain stock and real estate holdings.
Sen. Richard Shelby, the Alabama Republican who chairs the intelligence committee, said he hoped for an early Senate vote on Tenet's nomination.
"I wish we could have done this earlier, but we had to wait out the process," he said. "We think it will move fast."
Clinton nominated Tenet after Anthony Lake, the president's former national security adviser, withdrew his nomination for the CIA post in frustration over the confirmation process.
Shelby said he spoke with Tenet, currently CIA deputy director, before the vote was taken.
"He feels good about this, he's glad it's over with, we are too," Shelby said.

The investigation focused on telephone stock and condominium apartments in Greece that Tenet inherited from his father, who died in 1983. Tenet did not list those items on his initial financial disclosure forms when he joined the Clinton administration. Tenet said he did not learn about the stock and Athens property until 1994.
